content.text: Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Legal status:
part of the patient's identification data.
Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Admitting diagnosis:
a provisional or admitting diagnosis at admission, including intercurrent (medical) diseases as well as psychiatric diagnoses.
Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Reasons for admission:
clearly documented as stated by the patient and/or others significantly involved.
Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Social history:
social service records (interviews with the patient, family and others) assess home plans, family attitudes and community resource contacts, and include a social history.
Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Neuro exam:
when indicated, a complete neurological exam is recorded with the admission physical.
Intake (psychiatric hospital admission) — Psychiatric evaluation:

completed within 60 hours of admission, with a medical history, mental status, onset of illness and circumstances leading to admission, attitudes and behavior, estimates of intellectual functioning, memory and orientation, and an inventory of the patient's assets written descriptively, not interpretively.
Progress (treatment plan and progress notes) — Treatment plan:

an individual comprehensive plan based on the patient's strengths and disabilities, with a substantiated diagnosis, short-term and long-range goals, the specific treatment modalities, each team member's responsibilities, and documentation that justifies the diagnosis and treatment.
Progress (treatment plan and progress notes) — Progress notes:
at least weekly for the first 2 months and at least monthly after that, with recommendations for treatment-plan revisions and a precise assessment of progress against the plan.
Consult — Billing a consult (Medicare):
Medicare doesn't pay the CPT consultation codes (inpatient 99252-99255, office/outpatient 99242-99245); report the correct E/M visit code for the consult instead.
D/C (discharge summary) — Discharge summary:
a recap of the hospitalization, recommendations from appropriate services on follow-up or aftercare, and a brief summary of the patient's condition at discharge.
